semantics.mandatory_scope: All 42 requirements are mandatory within this candidate, subject only to their stated applicability conditions. This candidate is not ratified.
semantics.acceptance_cases: Scenarios and expected results specify future evidence obligations. They are not execution logs or passing test results.
semantics.evidence_kinds: Kinds describe different observation boundaries, not a universal ranking. Requirement-level minimum identifies the principal boundary; each case states any other boundary it needs.
semantics.applicability: A conditional subcase can be inapplicable only with a truthful capability/profile declaration. That does not exempt the entire pillar or an unconditional requirement.
semantics.claims: Record actual source/build/artifact, environment, method, result, direct evidence references and limits separately. Never infer a broader claim from a narrower journey.

evidence_kind_definitions.source_inspection: Inspection of exact versioned declarations, source references and current/historical evidence pointers; does not prove execution.
evidence_kind_definitions.controlled_integration: Executed deterministic scenario with explicit real-versus-synthetic boundaries; does not imply native, installed or independent-network execution.
evidence_kind_definitions.runtime_integration: Observed supported runtime/storage/adapter integration for the declared scenario; exact platform/process/network scope is recorded.
evidence_kind_definitions.owner_receipt: Authentic acceptance from the actual registry/board/memory owner, bound to the correct node, request revision/digest and scope; not a simulated fixture or a sent request.
evidence_kind_definitions.cross_surface_integration: Observed common capability or data contract through its declared UI/CLI/API/desktop mappings with matching authority and semantics.
evidence_kind_definitions.installed_package: Execution of the exact identified distributed artifact on the claimed platform; source execution or cross-build alone does not qualify.
evidence_kind_definitions.accessibility_inspection: Observed keyboard, focus, readable/status and supported assistive/reduced-motion interaction, with exact scope and any automated checks stated.
evidence_kind_definitions.claim_specific_journey: Direct evidence for an additional claim such as consumer downloaded launch, independent machines/networks or human acceptance; the actual boundary must be named.
evidence_kind_definitions.schema_fixture: Executed schema/record-shape validation only; does not prove behavior.
evidence_kind_definitions.native_runtime: Observed native storage/transport/runtime components with environment and process scope explicit.
evidence_kind_definitions.independent_devices: Observed interaction between separately running physical or virtual installations; name devices and network scope.
evidence_kind_definitions.independent_networks: Observed interaction across independently administered networks; record actual route and supported journey.
evidence_kind_definitions.human_acceptance: Actual named owner/user acceptance for the stated journey; not inferred from agent test completion.

requirements.requirement: Keep authoritative accepted domain history in append-only, cryptographically hashed and authenticated ledgers transferable to authorized peers; identify authoritative, staged, derived, cached and secret stores.
requirements.applicability: Every node. Secret-key custody is separate from transferable domain history; an independently verified ledger adapter may provide record signatures rather than a redundant per-event signature.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Append domain records, restart, transfer retained records to a second authorized instance and verify them.
acceptance_cases.expected: Stable record/resource/writer identities and authenticated history verify; derived state is not substituted for missing authoritative records.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Tamper with a record, present an unauthorized writer or unexpected fork/truncation.
acceptance_cases.expected: Reject or quarantine according to declared policy; preserve last accepted history and evidence; do not silently reset identity or reinterpret history.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Inspect the persistence map and transferable export.
acceptance_cases.expected: All recovery-essential stores are classified; private signing keys and bearer secrets are excluded from ordinary peer transfer.

requirements.evidence_limit: Verified retained records establish the stated origin/history integrity, not truthful content, permanent availability, public disclosure authorization or a new DID method.

requirements.requirement: Preserve accepted local intent and original media bytes durably through interruption, and reconcile uncertain writes by stable operation/content identity before claiming them saved.
requirements.applicability: Every node for accepted local intent. Original-byte cases apply whenever the node accepts assets, recordings or other dependent content; absence of asset capabilities does not exempt the intent requirement.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Interrupt before append, after append before receipt, and during retry; restart the supported runtime.
acceptance_cases.expected: Intent survives supported interruption; reconciliation yields one logical operation and no silently discarded pending work.

acceptance_cases.scenario: When assets are accepted, fail their primary save after the UI can render them, then recreate the renderer/service.
acceptance_cases.expected: Original bytes remain recoverable in a durable spool or primary store and retry to verified locators; metadata-only success is not reported as complete save.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Apply storage pressure while the last durable original is still needed.
acceptance_cases.expected: Explicit backpressure/recovery state preserves that copy or refuses acceptance honestly; cache eviction cannot silently lose accepted originals.

requirements.evidence_limit: A durable metadata record or visible cached image does not prove durable original bytes; this requirement does not assert power-loss semantics beyond the declared store guarantee.

requirements.requirement: Declare and demonstrate rebuilding supported projections from retained authoritative inputs, assets, permission cuts and verified snapshots with explicit schema/projection versions.
requirements.applicability: Every node with materialized state. A node that exposes only its ledger still declares interpretation, retained scope and verification of any index/checkpoint it uses.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Remove only a disposable projection/index and rebuild through the supported recovery operation.
acceptance_cases.expected: The declared state and relevant permission cut agree with the pre-rebuild state; keys and authoritative records are preserved.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Supply a snapshot with wrong source cut/digest/version or with required inputs unavailable.
acceptance_cases.expected: Reject the snapshot or expose precise incomplete recovery; do not label a partial state complete.

requirements.evidence_limit: Rebuild equivalence is limited to declared retained inputs and versions; a snapshot hash does not establish availability of omitted history or assets.

requirements.requirement: Express corrections, supersession, permission changes and migrations as new attributable records; preserve original signatures and schema meaning or an explicit verifiable transformation.
requirements.applicability: Every node. Authoritative history and required audit records remain append-only. Ephemeral diagnostics are classified at collection time; any separately authorized replica availability change preserves provenance and discloses missing coverage. This standard grants no deletion authority.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Correct an accepted record and migrate a supported older schema.
acceptance_cases.expected: New records link to the prior record/version; original evidence remains interpretable and current projection reflects the authorized correction.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Interrupt migration or replay a migration request.
acceptance_cases.expected: Resume/reconcile idempotently or retain the prior usable state; do not silently truncate history, duplicate accepted transformations or switch identity.

requirements.evidence_limit: A tombstone, migration or local erasure cannot recall copies already shared; migration evidence covers only declared source/target versions and retained scope.

requirements.requirement: Maintain a distinct Hapa Kanban Board bound to the node definition, accountable owner and declared visibility, with links to its repository and adoption work.
requirements.applicability: Every independently governed node definition, including each distinct node in a monorepo. Shared board infrastructure is allowed; supporting libraries alone are not separate nodes.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Resolve the node's declared board through the actual board owner.
acceptance_cases.expected: An owner-accepted board identity and node binding match the repository/manifest; node-specific work is discoverable.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Restart registration or encounter an unavailable board owner.
acceptance_cases.expected: Reconcile the same board/binding without duplicates; unavailable access is reported separately from the existing accepted binding.

requirements.evidence_limit: A GitHub issue or local board intent is not proof that the Hapa Board exists; board history records work and evidence, not runtime execution permission.

requirements.requirement: Register the node with Hapa Quest Keeper using an accepted binding for its identity, owner, purpose, capabilities, board and lifecycle state.
requirements.applicability: Every node definition; private installation-level entries, if used, have separate scope and disclosure policy.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Submit or reconcile a real node registration with the owner-supported adapter.
acceptance_cases.expected: A verifiable owner receipt binds the actual node, service, request revision/digest and accepted scope; retain its record reference.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Present a receipt for another node, service, revision or request digest.
acceptance_cases.expected: It cannot fulfill this registration; the mismatch is explicit and the correct intent remains pending/rejected as appropriate.

requirements.evidence_limit: Sending a request, writing a local manifest or naming Quest Keeper is not acceptance; registration does not certify the listed capabilities.

requirements.requirement: Distinguish registration intent, accepted binding, freshness and current reachability; use durable idempotent reconciliation with bounded retries.
requirements.applicability: Every node and every required registry/board integration.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Make registry owners unavailable, queue changes, restart and reconnect.
acceptance_cases.expected: Supported local work continues; durable intents reconcile once to the actual acceptance state without duplicate boards/entries or lost revisions.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Lose an acceptance reply and retry the same operation, then submit genuinely changed content.
acceptance_cases.expected: Identical intent reconciles to the same binding/revision; changed content gets a new revision and truthful status.

requirements.evidence_limit: A previously accepted binding does not imply current reachability; a failed reachability probe does not by itself revoke the binding.

requirements.requirement: Provide a usable UI, CLI, API and desktop shell for the node's declared capabilities and supported platform profiles.
requirements.applicability: Every independently operating node. The desktop shell may reuse a supported host/client, and an API may be local; libraries are not used to disguise operating nodes.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Launch the supported desktop package and operate a representative capability through UI, CLI and API.
acceptance_cases.expected: All four surfaces are available with documented entry points, the same node/resource binding and inspectable outcomes.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Use a declared reduced runtime profile or unavailable native dependency.
acceptance_cases.expected: The exact unavailable capability and recovery path are visible; the node does not claim full parity for that profile.

requirements.evidence_limit: A source directory, build script or screenshot does not establish a working surface; reduced portable/browser profiles do not silently waive the main node's four surfaces.

requirements.requirement: Maintain semantic feature/capability parity, including permissions, validation, outcomes and status, across the four interaction surfaces.
requirements.applicability: Every declared node capability. Visual gestures may map to semantic commands; temporary gaps remain adoption gaps, not self-issued exceptions.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Execute each declared capability's common valid/invalid fixtures through its surface mappings.
acceptance_cases.expected: Results, validation, side effects and permission decisions agree; the capability matrix identifies the exact operation on each surface.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Attempt a restricted or destructive action through CLI/API after UI rejection.
acceptance_cases.expected: The alternative surface cannot bypass the same authority or declared confirmation policy.

requirements.evidence_limit: Parity concerns authorized capability and outcome, not pixel-identical layouts; a representative scenario alone cannot certify untested capabilities.

requirements.requirement: Publish a versioned typed capability contract with stable IDs, input/output/error schemas, permission scope, side effects, idempotency, cancellation and runtime requirements.
requirements.applicability: Every node and exposed capability; one implementation can serve multiple surfaces.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Discover capabilities and validate supported calls/responses through each mapped adapter.
acceptance_cases.expected: Schemas, versions and runtime requirements are inspectable and match behavior; unknown capabilities/versions fail explicitly.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Send malformed, oversized or out-of-scope input.
acceptance_cases.expected: Bounded validation rejects it without uncontrolled resource use or unintended side effects; errors retain shared codes/meaning.

requirements.evidence_limit: A schema is a contract, not proof that every adapter implements it; a local API does not imply a public service endpoint.

requirements.requirement: Carry the standard repository documentation pack, including purpose, requirements, architecture, capabilities, persistence/recovery, permissions, operations, releases and conformance/adoption status.
requirements.applicability: Every repository containing a node definition; a monorepo indexes the pack for each governed node.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Follow README/contributor links through the required documentation pack.
acceptance_cases.expected: Each required topic and current owner/reference is present and understandable; supporting source/evidence is traceable.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Inspect broken, moved or restricted references and local-only operational instructions.
acceptance_cases.expected: The pack identifies unresolved/private locations without inventing content or implying unavailable documents were reviewed.

requirements.evidence_limit: A complete document pack does not certify implementation; inaccessible/private references must retain accurate visibility and ownership labels.

requirements.requirement: Preserve attributable 0-to-1 lineage from need and requirements through selected decisions, implementation, verification and current outcome, with supersession rather than invented history.
requirements.applicability: Every node, including legacy nodes reconstructing available provenance.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Trace a current capability backward to its requirement, selected decision, source/build and evidence.
acceptance_cases.expected: Known sources, dates/authors and supersession relationships are explicit, and generated summaries identify their source inputs and acceptance state.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Correct an earlier mistaken explanation or find missing origin history.
acceptance_cases.expected: Append a correction/link or mark the gap; do not rewrite an old observation as if it anticipated a later result.

requirements.evidence_limit: Reconstructed summaries are labeled as such; missing historical turns remain unknown. Private reasoning traces and secret material are not required documentation.

requirements.requirement: Maintain truthful current pointers and evidence-bound status while retaining historical reports; separate planned, implemented, verified and human-accepted claims.
requirements.applicability: Every node and conformance claim.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Compare current README/index/manifest links with the selected source/build/artifact and direct evidence.
acceptance_cases.expected: Current pointers agree; each claim names the boundary actually observed and preserves old reports as history.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Offer source-only or same-machine evidence for an installed, two-network or human acceptance claim.
acceptance_cases.expected: The stronger claim remains unverified; related success cannot upgrade the entire requirement or candidate.

requirements.evidence_limit: Documentation inspection verifies traceability, not the underlying behavior. Evidence levels and exact artifacts remain explicit.

requirements.requirement: Register the node's telemetry contract/catalog with Hapa Telemetry using an authentic accepted node/service binding and declared export/collection policy.
requirements.applicability: Every node definition; collection and instance export scopes remain separately authorized.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Resolve the actual telemetry registration.
acceptance_cases.expected: Owner receipt binds the node, catalog/schema version and accepted scope; configured adapters/export policy match its declaration.

acceptance_cases.scenario: The collector becomes unavailable or registration is still pending.
acceptance_cases.expected: Local status remains inspectable and truthful; normal authorized domain work continues without a fabricated accepted registration.

requirements.evidence_limit: Telemetry registration does not authorize external access to private payloads or prove that every metric is instrumented.

requirements.requirement: Use the shared vocabulary, units and correlation fields for lifecycle, operation, connection, storage, recovery and I/O observations; namespace domain-specific extensions.
requirements.applicability: Every node; unavailable measurements remain explicitly unknown/not instrumented rather than zero or success.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Capture a bounded operation/connection/recovery journey and inspect UI, API and exported observations.
acceptance_cases.expected: Node/build/protocol, operation/attempt/resource correlation, stage, measurement basis and error meanings agree across outputs.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Encounter unknown route, missing size, reset counter or skewed remote clock.
acceptance_cases.expected: Use unknown/epoch/basis fields; do not invent zero throughput, verified relay use or exact one-way latency.

requirements.evidence_limit: Telemetry is an observation with defined basis and scope; it does not independently prove a peer's truthfulness or global state.

requirements.requirement: Declare privacy, collection/export scope, instrumentation coverage, sampling, retention and resource bounds; expose gaps and enforce redaction before persistence/export.
requirements.applicability: Every node and telemetry adapter, including local-only collection.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Exercise sensitive input and export a diagnostic/telemetry sample.
acceptance_cases.expected: Secrets, private payload bodies and disallowed endpoint/path details are absent by default; exported scope follows the declared policy.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Flood or disable a collector and reach retention/storage limits.
acceptance_cases.expected: Queues/retries/storage remain bounded, omissions are visible and domain progress is not blocked by optional telemetry export.

requirements.evidence_limit: Redacted telemetry is not a complete domain transcript; declared coverage and sampling limits accompany derived claims.

requirements.requirement: Maintain authentic accepted Second Brain and Hapa Wiki entries binding the node, owner, canonical source, provenance and current standard/adoption references.
requirements.applicability: Every node definition; private entries and public projections may have different authorized scopes.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Resolve both actual node entries through their owners.
acceptance_cases.expected: Accepted bindings and record references match the node and declared visibility; documentation/provenance links are correct.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Present a stale or other-node acceptance receipt or an unavailable projection.
acceptance_cases.expected: Registration, content revision and reachability are distinguished; the wrong receipt cannot fulfill the current binding.

requirements.evidence_limit: A repository file or local update intent is not proof of live Second Brain/Wiki acceptance; a public index need not expose private source content.

requirements.requirement: Create durable, attributable documentation/memory update intents for meaningful requirement, architecture, capability, protocol, release, incident and conformance changes.
requirements.applicability: Every node; high-frequency telemetry samples are not individual documentation triggers.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Produce a meaningful change while the destination is offline, restart, reconnect and lose one acknowledgment.
acceptance_cases.expected: One stable update intent survives and reconciles to the correct revision without duplicate entries; pending/accepted outcomes stay distinct.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Emit many routine telemetry samples and then correct a prior summary.
acceptance_cases.expected: Samples are bounded/coalesced rather than creating task floods; correction preserves the prior source-linked history.

requirements.evidence_limit: A trigger proves work was queued, not that a memory or Wiki update was accepted. Generated summaries retain their own provenance and review state.

requirements.requirement: Maintain explicit custody, ownership, visibility and allowed disclosure for node documentation and memory; keep private source material out of broader syndication.
requirements.applicability: Every node, generated summary and destination projection.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Syndicate a node update with restricted source/evidence to authorized private and public projections.
acceptance_cases.expected: Each destination receives only allowed content; public references preserve access boundaries and source ownership.

acceptance_cases.scenario: A generated summary or imported trigger requests a broader disclosure or claims owner authority.
acceptance_cases.expected: Existing authorization boundaries remain enforced; untrusted content cannot grant publication permission.

requirements.evidence_limit: A destination link or accepted entry is not permission to copy private content to another audience; summaries do not erase original custody.

requirements.requirement: Provide collapsed, expanded and hidden I/O Bar modes, top/bottom placement, pause/resume display and a discoverable restore path, with persistent per-device preferences.
requirements.applicability: Every node UI and desktop shell; CLI/API expose equivalent preference and inspection operations.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Move, expand, collapse, pause, hide, restore and restart the app.
acceptance_cases.expected: Controls work, preferences survive appropriately and the bar does not obscure critical content or lose the user's input/focus.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Traffic continues while hidden/paused, then the user returns to live view.
acceptance_cases.expected: Display truthfully shows pause/age and offers jump-to-live without replaying an unbounded animation backlog or changing permissions.

requirements.evidence_limit: Hiding/pausing is a view setting; it neither stops traffic nor silently changes collection, telemetry export or domain persistence.

requirements.requirement: Classify I/O with separate relationship, locality, path, direction and plane fields; derive LOCAL, P2P and SERVICE colors/labels and preserve OTHER/UNKNOWN when unproven.
requirements.applicability: Every instrumented I/O adapter. Local-storage or infrastructure events are labeled separately from application peer exchanges.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Observe local Hapa exchange, remote direct peer exchange, relayed peer exchange and centralized API traffic.
acceptance_cases.expected: Headline classes retain their meanings; relay path is a separate badge and centralized authority is not hidden by transport choice.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Use an unknown peer binding, gateway-terminated trust boundary or uninstrumented path.
acceptance_cases.expected: Unknown/other and known limitations remain visible; no guessed verified-local or P2P claim is emitted.

requirements.evidence_limit: Color is a presentation of known facts, not a trust proof. A configured relay, loopback proxy or shared IP prefix does not establish actual route, locality or Hapa identity.

requirements.requirement: Represent queued, sent, received, verified, admitted, applied, durable, remote-receipt and retention observations distinctly and link each to the evidence actually available.
requirements.applicability: Every I/O observation; absent stages stay unknown and are not inferred from a later-looking label.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Feed observations for sent-without-reply, local durability, verified blocks and an explicit scoped retention receipt.
acceptance_cases.expected: Each produces only its permitted claim with observer/recipient/content scope; the timeline does not overwrite incomparable facts into one success ladder.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Time out after a possibly durable write or exclude a durable contribution by an admission cut.
acceptance_cases.expected: Show pending/unknown or durable-but-excluded correctly; retry retains operation identity and cancellation does not imply rollback.

requirements.evidence_limit: Transport handoff does not prove remote application acceptance; signed head is not block possession; a retention promise is not guaranteed future availability.

requirements.requirement: Define rate windows, units and measurement boundaries; distinguish unique operations, attempts, recipient deliveries, payload bytes and wire bytes without double counting.
requirements.applicability: Every displayed or exported counter/rate; unknown size or unsupported measurement is explicitly labeled.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Send one operation to several recipients with retries and overlapping upper/lower-layer observations.
acceptance_cases.expected: Unique operation count remains one; recipient/attempt counts and real transmitted bytes are separate; incompatible byte bases are not summed.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Restart counters, drop samples, batch events or omit sizes.
acceptance_cases.expected: Epoch/reset and coverage are explicit; no negative rate or exact-looking invented measurement appears.

requirements.evidence_limit: A rate is valid only for its stated observer, window, counter epoch and byte basis; cross-node timestamps alone do not prove one-way latency.

requirements.requirement: Expose safe typed identity, endpoint, ledger and evidence references with appropriate redaction and deliberate navigation; exclude secrets and private payload capture by default.
requirements.applicability: Every I/O row, detail view, copied field, URL action and export.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Inspect and export representative local/private/public events containing identity and endpoint references.
acceptance_cases.expected: References retain correct type and scope; allowed details are inspectable while secrets, invitations and private data remain redacted.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Supply a credential-bearing URL, executable scheme, attacker-controlled label or capability-bearing link.
acceptance_cases.expected: Render as inert safe text or require the declared deliberate action; do not auto-fetch/execute, leak credentials or invent a resolver.

requirements.evidence_limit: A Hypercore key is not automatically a DID; a URL is not authenticated identity. Revealing a reference locally does not authorize exporting it.

requirements.requirement: Make I/O Bar meaning and controls accessible beyond color and motion, with keyboard operation, readable labels, focus handling and reduced-motion behavior.
requirements.applicability: Every UI and desktop shell embedding the I/O Bar.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Use keyboard controls and a supported assistive inspection with motion disabled/system reduced-motion enabled.
acceptance_cases.expected: Controls have accessible names/state, essential information remains available statically and focus is usable on expand/close/hide/restore.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Sustain high event volume and narrow the viewport.
acceptance_cases.expected: No per-event announcement flood, flashing dependence or disappearing essential control; labels and detail navigation remain usable.

requirements.evidence_limit: A still screenshot or automated checker alone does not demonstrate keyboard, screen-reader or reduced-motion interaction.

requirements.requirement: Expose the same I/O observation/filter/detail and preference contract through UI, CLI and API, with the desktop shell using that contract.
requirements.applicability: Every node; semantic data parity does not require terminal animation.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Query one event set with equivalent filters through UI, CLI and API, then change a permitted display preference.
acceptance_cases.expected: Event identities, fields, receipt meanings and redaction agree; shell/UI preferences reflect the authorized change.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Attempt to reveal a field through CLI/API that the same user cannot inspect in UI.
acceptance_cases.expected: The same permission/disclosure rules apply; a different interaction surface is not a privilege escalation.

requirements.evidence_limit: Matching sampled outputs do not prove complete instrumentation; all surfaces retain the same coverage/unknown/redaction limits.

requirements.requirement: Separate authoritative domain history, retained append-only telemetry history and volatile display buffers; declare retention/coverage and bound queues, storage and recursive telemetry.
requirements.applicability: Every node and collector. Significant retained observations follow their ledger policy; high-rate ephemeral samples may be aggregated rather than retained individually.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Expand the ledger, follow an evidence link, restart and reach the declared retention boundary.
acceptance_cases.expected: Retained observations/proofs remain inspectable within scope; rotations/gaps and volatile versus durable status are explicit.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Flood I/O, stop the exporter and observe telemetry-export traffic itself.
acceptance_cases.expected: Memory/disk/retry remain bounded; sampling/drops are reported; no recursive event explosion or blocked authorized domain action occurs.

requirements.evidence_limit: A ledger hash without retained payload is not a complete viewable log; losing sampled telemetry must not be confused with losing authoritative domain state.

requirements.requirement: Use typed node-definition, instance, subject, resource, writer, transport, session and service identities with explicit authenticated bindings and namespaces.
requirements.applicability: Every node. Existing legitimate identifiers are preserved; unsupported DID methods are not invented to satisfy this requirement.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Inspect a real capability/connection/record journey and resolve its typed bindings.
acceptance_cases.expected: The node, instance, resource, authority, writer and transport are unambiguous and each claimed authenticated binding has actual evidence.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Substitute a same-name subject, another resource's feed or a new endpoint under an old service label.
acceptance_cases.expected: The substitution cannot inherit authority or stale endpoint evidence without an explicit valid binding/adoption revision.

requirements.evidence_limit: Display names, discovery keys, endpoints and successful connections do not by themselves establish authority or membership.

requirements.requirement: Declare and support identity continuity, backup/recovery and authorized key rotation independently of networking/provider changes.
requirements.applicability: Every node instance with persistent authority or data; recovery procedures respect actual key custody and visibility.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Restart, restore a supported backup and replace an eligible provider.
acceptance_cases.expected: Persistent subject/resource/writer identities and historical verification remain stable according to the declared policy.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Attempt unbound key rotation or present a conflicting recovery lineage.
acceptance_cases.expected: Reject/quarantine or invoke the documented authorized recovery path; do not silently mint a replacement identity to clear a connection error.

requirements.evidence_limit: A new endpoint/key cannot self-authorize continuity; documented recovery is not proof against compromise outside the declared trust policy.

requirements.requirement: Bind operations, invitations, channels and records to application namespace, resource, role and compatible protocol; enforce host/secret boundaries and authenticated scoped authorization.
requirements.applicability: Every node's local and remote interfaces, including loopback bridges and replicas.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Authenticate an authorized request and attempt cross-resource, expired-invitation and out-of-role operations.
acceptance_cases.expected: Only allowed scope is admitted; connection/discovery success cannot grant arbitrary feed replication or domain permissions.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Use an unauthorized origin/session capability at a loopback/native boundary.
acceptance_cases.expected: Reject it despite local transport; renderer/export content cannot obtain root secrets or arbitrary host operations.

requirements.evidence_limit: Cryptographic origin does not establish legal domain behavior; a replica may serve valid history without authority to act as its author.

requirements.requirement: Deduplicate stable mutating operation identities and reconcile admission at execution/commit boundaries, preserving locally durable but excluded intent for honest recovery.
requirements.applicability: Every node mutating capability and queued authoritative write.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Repeat a write before/after lost acknowledgment and reuse its ID with conflicting content.
acceptance_cases.expected: Identical intent returns the same reconciled operation/position; conflict is rejected rather than reauthored or duplicated.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Change admission while work is queued and while a write becomes durable.
acceptance_cases.expected: Recheck/reconcile accurately; receipt distinguishes local durability from admitted state, and excluded work remains recoverable without bypassing revocation.

requirements.evidence_limit: Idempotency is scoped to declared identity/resource/payload semantics; local append durability does not establish accepted contribution or remote retention.

requirements.requirement: Bound startup/readiness and request lifetimes, settling each runtime generation on ready, fatal error, early exit, timeout and shutdown.
requirements.applicability: Every node with asynchronous initialization, host processes or pending requests.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Exit before first ready, never become ready and fail during the initial operation; then start a healthy replacement.
acceptance_cases.expected: Original callers settle or recover within the declared bound, replacement work succeeds and no promise depends on a retired readiness source.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Deliver late ready/reply events from a retired generation.
acceptance_cases.expected: They cannot settle or mutate the current generation; pending maps/timers and diagnostics stay consistent.

requirements.evidence_limit: Controlled lifecycle evidence does not establish every platform's installed startup behavior; targeted installed qualification is separate.

requirements.requirement: Apply one consistent activation/cancellation ownership rule across initial actions, reconnect, resend, delayed completion and persisted recovery.
requirements.applicability: Every cancellable/connectable session or asynchronous authority transition.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Hold initialization, cancel, reconnect/resend, release delayed work and restart.
acceptance_cases.expected: A cancelled generation cannot first-activate local or remote authority, leak a reservation or mutate the next attempt; fresh work remains possible.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Lose an acknowledgment for an already established activation and reconnect.
acceptance_cases.expected: Legitimate idempotent recovery succeeds without a second authority or weakening cancellation/admission checks.

requirements.evidence_limit: Cancellation does not erase a previously committed effect; disconnect/presence expiry does not by itself prove concession, departure or loss.

requirements.requirement: Drain durable queues reliably across concurrent enqueue, failures and runtime recovery, with bounded backpressure and without requiring another user action to flush final work.
requirements.applicability: Every node with queued mutation, media, registration or documentation work.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Enqueue additional work during multiple awaited steps of an active drain, release the work and stop input.
acceptance_cases.expected: All eligible final items progress without extra edit/reload; stable identity and ordering requirements remain intact.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Interrupt the worker, restore it and exhaust declared queue/storage bounds.
acceptance_cases.expected: Recovery is idempotent with bounded retry; pressure and rejected/pending work are explicit rather than silently lost.

requirements.evidence_limit: A drained local queue does not by itself prove remote application acceptance; each queue uses its own truthful receipt semantics.

requirements.requirement: Select new service operations from current adopted policy with explicit role, overlay, provenance, expiry/disable/retirement and descriptor-scoped evidence; preserve identity and existing valid data.
requirements.applicability: Every node's configured bootstrap, relay, replica/archive, gateway and other replaceable providers; unused roles need no deployment.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Expire/disable/retire a provider after startup and attempt a new eligible operation.
acceptance_cases.expected: Selection uses current policy and reports no eligible route where appropriate; retired defaults do not resurrect silently.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Change a provider key/endpoint under the same service ID and interrupt a policy import.
acceptance_cases.expected: Caches/evidence bind the actual descriptor; incomplete imports do not masquerade as completed adoption or reset identity/history.

requirements.evidence_limit: A selected/dialed relay is not observed carriage; expiry of discovery policy need not tear down an otherwise authorized healthy application session.

requirements.requirement: Declare supported runtime/transport profiles and adapter guarantees for framing, authentication, authorization, backpressure, cancellation and recovery; keep application rules outside generic transport.
requirements.applicability: Every node, including offline/browser-only profiles. Unsupported transports or facilities are explicit; no new operated VPS is implied.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Exercise each declared profile's supported connection/operation and an incompatible profile/version.
acceptance_cases.expected: Supported adapters enforce their contract; incompatibility is visible and does not cause silent insecure fallback or identity change.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Offer an alternative provider/transport whose framing or trust termination differs.
acceptance_cases.expected: Use a declared verified adapter or reject it; do not assume stream compatibility or hide gateway authority behind a P2P label.

requirements.evidence_limit: Native/local or fixture success does not prove public-service availability, every NAT topology or a browser's ability to use native UDP.

requirements.requirement: Provide an authorized verifiable transfer/export and supported restore path for domain history, required assets, interpretation versions and declared ownership/recovery scope.
requirements.applicability: Every node. A node with no accepted assets declares that fact; nodes that accept assets must include them or report explicit incompleteness.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Export/transfer the declared scope and restore it in a second supported instance.
acceptance_cases.expected: Required records/assets verify and state is usable with accurate identity/ownership semantics; export names its versions and completeness.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Omit/corrupt an asset, exceed a bound or interrupt transfer.
acceptance_cases.expected: Report specific missing/invalid scope and recover safely; do not label partial content self-contained or complete.

requirements.evidence_limit: A verified transfer is not proof of future retention or a backup of secret keys; export completeness and private-key recovery have separate policies.

requirements.requirement: Provide targeted installed-release qualification for each claimed supported desktop platform, bound to actual artifact/source identities, startup, data placement and supported reopen/recovery behavior.
requirements.applicability: Every claimed desktop release/platform. Separate independent-network qualification is required only when the node makes that stronger reachability/product-readiness claim; it is not substituted for platform qualification.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Install/open the exact released artifact on each claimed platform, exercise a core capability, close and reopen.
acceptance_cases.expected: Artifact digest/source/environment are recorded; native startup, data outside replaceable install assets, identity and domain-state persistence meet the declared profile.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Exercise a relevant bounded startup/dependency failure in the installed candidate.
acceptance_cases.expected: Failure/recovery is visible and finite, and accepted data/identity remain intact; missing mandatory reports prevent a passing platform claim.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Publish a broader consumer-launch, independent-network or human acceptance claim.
acceptance_cases.expected: Attach direct evidence for that additional boundary and exact candidate, or label it unverified; same-machine public-DHT traffic cannot stand in for two networks.

requirements.evidence_limit: Cross-building is not execution. Hosted VM execution is not ordinary consumer download handling, two independent networks or human acceptance; report those separately when claimed.

requirements.requirement: Pin an inspectable complete standard bundle and lock to its canonical Second Brain authority/provenance, exact version/content and adoption state; separate bootstrap source publication from ledger acceptance.
requirements.applicability: Every node repository. Initial draft mirrors may be bootstrap source only while authentic authority/ledger bindings remain pending.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Compare repository mirror/lock with the referenced immutable bundle and inspect its authority/adoption state.
acceptance_cases.expected: All pinned files/digests and version match; canonical source and actual acceptance/ratification status are explicit.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Interrupt a mirror update or mix old schemas with a new document.
acceptance_cases.expected: Expose/reject incomplete mixed state; retain a complete verified bundle rather than a misleading successful lock.

requirements.evidence_limit: An ordinary Git commit or copied standard is not a Second Brain ledger receipt, ratification, implementation or conformance certification.

requirements.requirement: Implement inspectable recurring standards, mirror, registration and documentation reconciliation with configured cadence, trigger/catch-up behavior, bounded retry and visible check state.
requirements.applicability: Every responsible node/repository/governance scheduler according to the standard's ownership matrix. A written schedule alone is not an activated scheduler.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Run the configured due/triggered checks and inspect recorded last attempt, success, due time, observed release and result.
acceptance_cases.expected: Checks occur under the actual scheduler; drift generates one deduplicated bounded task/proposal, not an unapproved behavioral upgrade.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Remain offline across several intervals, change the clock or repeatedly fail a destination.
acceptance_cases.expected: Perform one appropriate catch-up with jitter/backoff, keep last verified state and mark unknown freshness; no retry storm or blocked app startup occurs.

requirements.evidence_limit: A successful check observes current reachable metadata at a time; it does not prove no unseen later release. Offline periods cannot perform runtime checks.

requirements.requirement: Verify authorized release integrity and continuity across the entire bundle; separate discovery/caching/proposal from adoption, code execution, disclosure changes and migrations.
requirements.applicability: Every standards distribution/adoption adapter. Bootstrap unsigned/unbound source stays explicitly unverified for automated trusted adoption until the actual owner binding is established.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Fetch the same authorized release through two permitted mirrors and propose adoption.
acceptance_cases.expected: Complete bundle identity and trusted authority verify; proposal preserves existing operation/permissions until the authorized adoption policy applies.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Offer tampered files, same-version different bytes, rollback, unbound key rotation or conflicting signed branch.
acceptance_cases.expected: Reject/quarantine and preserve conflict evidence; no downloaded code runs or telemetry scope expands merely from a release notification.

requirements.evidence_limit: A familiar URL, newer version string or valid untrusted signature is not standards authority; this requirement does not claim implementation of any external secure-update framework.

requirements.requirement: Record requirement-level adoption gaps/deviations with owner, reason, scope, target and evidence; preserve old claims and require an authorized adoption record for changed conformance.
requirements.applicability: Every node adopting or claiming a standard version; no node can silently waive a mandatory candidate requirement.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Adopt a candidate with known gaps, then fix one requirement and update its evidence.
acceptance_cases.expected: Only the supported requirement/build claim changes; remaining gaps stay explicit and historical standard/evidence versions remain intact.

acceptance_cases.scenario: Copy the standard, mark difficult requirements not applicable without a rule, or infer pass from a related journey.
acceptance_cases.expected: No meets-standard claim is accepted; applicability and the exact evidence boundary must be justified for each mandatory requirement.

requirements.evidence_limit: A recorded deviation explains a gap but does not make it conformant. A draft target and declarative case catalog are not executed results or ratified policy.
